To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The transit time of the intestinal contents is faster in GF chicks than in CV chicks; the accumulation of Ca is greater in CV chicks; and the secretion of Ca into the intestinal lume is similar in both groups but the amount appearing within the gut wall is greater in CV.
the transit time of the digesta in the germfree birds was appreciablly faster than in the conventional controls, and that the accumulation of Ca was much greater in the conventional birds.
the transit time of gut contents in the GF chicks is faster than in the conventional chicks and that the rate of Ca removal from the gut wall is slower in the GF group than in the CV chicks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the absorption of calcium from the gastrointestinal tract of the chick.
the absorption and secretion of Ca in the gastrointestinal tract.
the effect of the intestinal microflora on the uptake, secretion and transport of Ca in the gastrointestinal tract (GIT) of the chick.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the absence of the microbial load does not alter the ability of the intestinal epithelium to absorb Ca but does alter the rate of its removal from the gut wall.
the microbial load of the gut is important in the control of Ca metabolism in the chick.
the microbial load does affect the absorption and secretion of Ca in the chick, but the mechanism by which this occurs remains to be established.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in GF chicks there is a slower rate of transit of digesta in both the small and the large intestine, a greater accumulation of Ca in enterocytes in the ileum and a greater retention of Ca within the enterocyte.
the microbial flora of the gut is important in the control of Ca absorption and secretion but that it does not affect the uptake of Ca by the enterocyte.
the absence of micro-organisms does not affect the absorption of Ca from the intestinal lumen but the rate of removal of Ca from the wall of the intestine is slower in germ-free animals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of the microbial load does not alter the ability of the chick enterocytes to absorb calcium.
the gut microbial load has a profound impact on the absorption and secretion of Ca in the chick.

there is no effect of the absence of microbes on the absorption of calcium by enterocytes in the chick, but the subsequent removal from the enterocytes to the blood stream is slower in the absence of microbes.
